input.question: if DNA is being damaged as you get older how can an old man, and there is cases of people with 80 years old or more, have a son and this son is like all other babies, new and fresh?
input.ground_truth: It's all thanks to a wonderful enzyme called telomerase. DNA gets shorter every time it divides, so it has long non coding regions on the ends called telomeres. These shorten too, but because they aren't essential for making anything they don't damage you until they actually run out. When producing sperm and eggs telomerase is active and gives each bit of DNA brand new telomeres even as the older people have telomeres that run out. Plants have telomerase activity at their growth nodes throughout their entire life, which is why when you take cuttings those are new and fresh too.

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine DNA is like a special instruction book inside every cell that tells your body how to grow and work. When you get older, sometimes this book can get a few little mistakes or tiny tears, kind of like when a page in your favorite storybook gets crumpled.

But when a grown-up man (even if he is 80 years old or more) wants to have a baby, his body makes special cells just for making a baby. These special cells try very hard to fix any mistakes in the DNA before they help make a new baby.

So, when the old man’s special baby-making cell joins with the mother’s special baby-making cell, they both work together to fix any little mistakes as much as they can. That’s why the new baby is born fresh and healthy, with a new instruction book that doesn’t have all the mistakes the dad’s old cells have. It’s like making a brand new, clean copy from the old, crumpled one!

That’s how an old man can have a healthy, new baby.
